info.title: MonitorFlow public API
info.description: Scripts and integrations use `/api/v1` with an API key made under Admin › API keys: `Authorization: Bearer mfk_…`. A key acts as the administrator who made it, within its reach (everything, a customer or a site), its access and its areas. Lists that can grow take `limit` and `cursor` and answer `next_cursor`, null on the last page. Every error has `error`, plain words, and `code`, stable. Writes may carry `Idempotency-Key`; the same request again within 24 hours gets the first answer with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`. A key makes up to 600 requests a minute; answers carry `RateLimit-Limit`, `RateLimit-Remaining` and `RateLimit-Reset`, and 429 carries `Retry-After`. See ADR-0101.

get.description:
The campaigns of the customers the caller reads as a whole, newest
first, without their batches and servers (read one for those).
Campaigns are never deleted.

Needs any role on the customer as a whole (everything or the customer;
a role on one site, or a key that reaches one site, sees none) and the
key area "updates". Paginated with `limit` and `cursor`; unknown
parameters and bad values are 400.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: 1 to 500, default 100.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: `next_cursor` of the previous page.

401.description: No key, or a key that is unknown, expired or turned off: `unauthenticated`

403.description: The key's role or areas do not allow it: `forbidden` or `api_key_scope`

404.description: Not found, or outside the key's reach: `not_found`

429.description: Over the key's rate limit: `rate_limited`, with `Retry-After`

post.description:
Makes a `draft` campaign: nothing is sent to any server until it is
started. Its servers are frozen now: those of `server_ids` and the
unrevoked servers of `site_id`, all of the customer, sorted by host
name. A server added to the site later is not added to the campaign.
They are split into batches by `waves`, in order: explicit server
lists first, then `{"size": n}` and `{"percent": p}` (of all servers,
rounded up) take the next servers by host name; the servers left form
one last batch. Without `waves`, one batch.

Once started, each server gets one signed command, sent when its agent
is connected and has no other command in flight:

- a package update (`apply_updates` with `packages`, `security_only`
  and `allow_reboot`; empty `packages` upgrades everything). A server
  whose agent does not accept package updates is left out of its
  batch. Where it can, MonitorFlow takes a local snapshot of the server
  first (`snapshot_command_id`). With `sources`, the server's package
  sources are first pointed at the pinned mirror snapshots and put back
  after the update (`sources_command_id`, `restore_command_id`); the
  central server needs mirrors and `mirror_public_url` for that;
- or, with `agent_version`, an agent update (`self_update`) to that
  version, which takes no package options.

These commands come from an administrator, so they are not classified
by the risk rules and need no approval.

Needs an administrator role on the customer as a whole and the key
area "updates". Audited as `campaign.create`. Not safe to repeat: send
`Idempotency-Key` to retry.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: 1 to 255 visible ASCII characters, a UUID usually. The same request again within 24 hours gets the first answer instead of running twice.

201.description: The draft, with its batches and servers

400.description: `invalid`, with `error` saying why: not the expected JSON, no `site_id` nor `server_ids`, `unknown site <id>` or `unknown server <id>` (not of the customer), `server <id> is revoked`, a bad name, `command_ttl_s` outside 60 to 604800, a bad package name, batch, window, time zone, failure threshold or pinned snapshot, `agent_version` not like `0.2.0`, or package options with `agent_version`

401.description: No key, or a key that is unknown, expired or turned off: `unauthenticated`

403.description: `forbidden`: the caller reads the customer without administering it as a whole. `api_key_scope`: the key lacks the area

404.description: `not_found`: a customer the caller does not read

409.description: `conflict`, with `sources` only: `mirror_public_url is not configured`, `mirrors are not enabled on this server`, or the mirrors' signing key cannot be used

429.description: Over the key's rate limit: `rate_limited`, with `Retry-After`

get.description:
The campaign with its batches (`waves`) in order and, in each, its
servers with the status of their command: `pending` (no command yet),
`queued`, `sent`, `running`, `succeeded`, `failed`, `expired`,
`cancelled`, or `skipped` (no command, with `error` saying why, such as
`server revoked`). Poll it to follow a running campaign; the command of
each server is under `/commands/{command_id}`.

Needs any role on the campaign's customer as a whole and the key area
"updates".

post.description:
`scheduled` or `running` → `paused`: nothing more is queued, and the
campaign's commands still `queued` (not yet sent to the agent) are
cancelled; those already sent or running finish and count. Their
servers get a new command when the campaign is resumed.

Needs an administrator role on the customer as a whole and the key
area "updates". Audited as `campaign.pause`. Pausing a paused campaign
is 409.

post.description:
`paused` → `running`, or `scheduled` if no batch was queued yet. The
runner queues commands again, within the maintenance windows.

Needs an administrator role on the customer as a whole and the key
area "updates". Audited as `campaign.resume`. Resuming a campaign that
is not paused is 409.

post.description:
`draft` → `scheduled`. The campaign runner then queues the first
batch's commands as soon as a maintenance window is open for at least
60 more seconds (at once without windows), with an expiry no later
than the window's end, and the campaign becomes `running`. Each next
batch starts when every server of the one before has a result, unless
more of them failed than `failure_threshold`: the campaign is then
`failed` and its queued commands are cancelled. Past the last batch it
is `completed`.

Needs an administrator role on the customer as a whole and the key
area "updates". Audited as `campaign.start`. Starting again is 409.

post.description:
Any state but a final one → `stopped`, for good. Commands still
`queued` are cancelled; those already sent or running finish. A
stopped campaign cannot be started again: create another.

Needs an administrator role on the customer as a whole and the key
area "updates". Audited as `campaign.stop`. Stopping a `stopped`,
`completed` or `failed` campaign is 409.

incident_ids.description: 1 to [`MAX_LIMIT`] incidents, like a group of a notification.

Acknowledged.description:
Body of the answer: the incidents this request acknowledged. The
others were resolved, or someone acknowledged them first.

Aggregation.description: A simple aggregation across the selected series.

AiCommandsChange.description: The last `ai_commands` command of a server, in `GET /api/servers/{id}`.

requested_by.description: The username, `null` when the account is gone.

command.description: Runs this instead of the proposal, recorded as an `edit`.

agent_version.description: Set for an agent update campaign (ADR-0053).

command_ttl_s.description: Seconds a command may wait for its agent.

created_by.description: The user who made it; `null` once that user is deleted.

current_wave.description:
Index of the batch in progress, from 0; `null` before the first is
queued.

error.description: Why it stopped or failed; `null` otherwise.

site_id.description: The site named at creation; `null` when only `server_ids` were.

spec.description: What every package update installs (unused by an agent update).

CampaignDetail.description: `GET /api/campaigns/{id}` and the answer of every write.

CampaignFailureThreshold.description:
A wave fails when more of its servers failed than this. A failed
server is a command `failed`, `expired` or `cancelled`, or a server
skipped with an error. The default, `{"value": 0, "unit": "count"}`,
stops at the first failure.

CampaignFailureUnit.description: How a failure threshold counts: servers, or percent of the batch.

next_cursor.description: Pass as `cursor` for the next page; `null` on the last one.

CampaignPinnedMirror.description: A mirror and the published snapshot a campaign pins it to.

snapshot.description: One of its published snapshots, not `current`.

CampaignProgress.description:
Servers by status; `failed` includes expired commands and skipped
servers, `in_progress` queued, sent and running commands.

CampaignRequest.description:
Body of `POST /api/campaigns`. Only `customer_id`, `name` and a target
(`site_id` and/or `server_ids`) are required.

agent_version.description:
Update the agents to this version, like `0.3.1`, instead of
packages (ADR-0053); takes no package options nor `sources`.

allow_reboot.description: Whether the agent may reboot the server when an update needs it.

command_ttl_s.description:
Seconds a command may wait for its agent before it expires, 60 to
604800, default 3600; never past the end of the open window.

packages.description:
Packages to upgrade, up to 1000; empty upgrades everything. Names
are letters, digits and `.+_:-` not starting with `-`, or KB
numbers and update IDs for Windows servers.

server_ids.description: These servers of the customer, besides those of `site_id`.

site_id.description: Every unrevoked server of this site of the customer.

oneOf.description: Snapshots to pin every server to during its update (ADR-0038).

waves.description:
The batches, in order, up to 100; the servers left over make one
last batch. Empty: one batch of every server.

command_id.description:
The update command, see `/commands/{id}`; `null` before it is
queued.

exit_code.description: The update's exit code once it ran, else `null`.

snapshot_command_id.description: The local snapshot taken before the update, if any (ADR-0094).

sources_command_id.description:
With pinned snapshots: the `configure_sources` command before the
update and the command restoring the sources after it.

status.description:
`pending` (no command yet), `skipped` (no command, `error` says
why), or the command's state: `queued`, `sent`, `running`,
`succeeded`, `failed`, `expired`, `cancelled`. A failed restore of
pinned sources makes it `failed`.

CampaignSources.description:
The snapshots every server of a campaign installs from (ADR-0038):
each server uses the mirrors of its OS family.

mirrors.description: One or more mirrors, each once. Windows servers take no sources.

CampaignSourcesMode.description: How pinned sources treat a host's other sources (ADR-0032).

CampaignState.description: Where a campaign is. `stopped`, `completed` and `failed` are final.

CampaignUpdateSpec.description: The `ApplyUpdates` of every command of a campaign.

allow_reboot.description: Whether the agent may reboot the server when an update needs it.

packages.description: Packages to upgrade; empty upgrades everything.

oneOf.description: The next `n` servers by host name, `{"size": n}`.

size.description: The next `n` servers by host name, `{"size": n}`.

oneOf.description:
The next servers, `p` percent of all of them rounded up (1 to 100),
`{"percent": p}`.

percent.description:
The next servers, `p` percent of all of them rounded up (1 to 100),
`{"percent": p}`.

CampaignWaveSpec.description:
One wave as requested: explicit servers, a number of servers, or a
percentage of all targets (rounded up), taken in target order from
those no explicit wave names.

oneOf.description:
Every week on `weekdays` (ISO: 1 is Monday, 7 Sunday), from `start`
to `end` local time in `timezone` (IANA name). An `end` before
`start` closes the next day.

end.description: `HH:MM`, local time; `00:00` and `24:00` are the end of the day.

CampaignWindow.description:
When a campaign may queue commands. With no window, at any time; with
several, whenever one is open. At most 32.

CommandDetail.description:
`GET /api/commands/{id}`: the command and its output, each at most
the last 64 KiB.

health_timeout_s.description:
`self_update`: seconds the new agent has to connect before the
old one comes back; 30 to 3600, 300 by default.

packages.description: Packages to upgrade; empty or absent for all.

ttl_s.description:
Seconds the agent may still start it; [`MIN_TTL_S`] to
[`MAX_TTL_S`], default [`DEFAULT_TTL_S`].

parameters.description: The payload as JSON, for kinds the API knows.

site_count.description: Sites of the customer the user reads, not all of them.

command.description: What will run, or what was rejected.

details.description:
For instance `{"reason": "threshold_removed"}`, `{"notified":
true}` when a silence ended, `{"username", "via"}` when
acknowledged, or `{"step", "steps", "minutes", "told"}` for a
follow-up step.

kind.description:
`opened`, `escalated`, `deescalated`, `resolved`, what a silence
did: `silenced` and `silence_ended` (ADR-0079), `acknowledged`, and
`followed_up` when a follow-up step told someone (ADR-0082).

occurred_at.description: Sample time of the change, or the server clock without a sample.

severity.description: Severity after the change; `null` once resolved.

FollowUpView.description: Where an incident is in its follow-up.

next.description: Who it would tell then, people first; empty when nobody can be.

next_at.description: When the next step is told if nobody acknowledges.

started_at.description: When the first message went out.

state.description:
`waiting` for the next step at `next_at`, `silenced` until a silence
ends then waiting, or `stopped`.

step.description: Steps told so far, and how many there are now.

stop_reason.description:
When stopped: `acknowledged`, `resolved`, `not_critical`, or
`finished` once every step was told.

GroupView.description: A notification that told this incident with others (ADR-0080).

incidents.description:
How many incidents it told that the user may read, this one
included. Members on sites outside the user's scope are not counted.

GuestKind.description: What a Proxmox guest is, which picks its API path.

oneOf.description:
Who is told next if nobody acknowledges (ADR-0082); `null` when no
follow-up started: a warning, or not sent yet.

next_cursor.description: Pass as `cursor` for the next page; `null` on the last one.

IncidentView.description:
One incident. Field names and types are part of the API contract: add
fields, never rename or remove them.

acknowledged_by.description:
Who said they are on it, and when (ADR-0082); `null` until someone
does. The name stays when the account is removed.

can_acknowledge.description:
Whether the reader may acknowledge it: open, not acknowledged, and
the reader an operator or above of its site.

hostname.description: The server's hostname, or the relay's name.

instance.description: `""` for a series without an instance.

metric.description: `offline` when the server or relay stopped reporting (ADR-0072).

opened_at.description: Sample times, not the server clock.

peak_value.description: The worst value seen while open.

relay_id.description: Set for a relay's offline incident only (ADR-0072).

severity.description: `warning` or `critical`; the last one while resolved.

silenced.description: Whether a silence ever held back a notification of it.

silenced_until.description:
While open and covered by a silence, when the last one ends
(ADR-0079).

threshold.description: The threshold as it was when the incident opened.

PendingView.description:
One command waiting for approval. Field names and types are part of
the API contract: add fields, never rename or remove them.

can_approve.description:
Whether the user may approve this command as proposed, and reject
it. UX hints: the decision routes check again.

command.description: The proposed command, exactly as it would run.

commands_run.description: Commands the incident ran so far, and its limit.

deadline.description:
`opened_at + max_duration_s`: the incident escalates then, and a
decision after it is 409.

diagnosis.description: The AI's text: untrusted, shown as data.

id.description: The pending command; decisions go to `/approvals/{id}/...`.

shell.description:
What runs the command: `posix` (`/bin/sh`) or `powershell`
(Windows PowerShell), from the server's system (ADR-0084).

shell_acceptance.description:
What the server's agent last said it does with these commands:
`accepted`, `off`, `unsupported`, or `null` when unknown (ADR-0076).
Approving is 409 once it refuses them.

snapshots.description:
Whether a change on this server is snapshotted first, on Proxmox
(ADR-0044) or locally (ADR-0094); when not, rollback is limited.

tier.description: `low_impact` or `high_impact`, from the rules, never from the AI.

query.description: The PromQL the API ran, filters included.

reason.description: Sent back to the AI with the rejection, and recorded.

Rollup.description:
How each point of a range summarizes the samples since the previous
point. Without it, a point is the last sample before it, so a spike
between two points of a long range is not drawn.

SeriesView.description:
One series: its labels and its `[unix seconds, value]` points. A value
that is not finite is `null`.

oneOf.description:
The last time AI commands were turned on or off from the web
interface, `null` if never (ADR-0098).

The certificate issued last to this agent, revoked or not; `null`
when the CA never issued one (a server row created by hand).

ServerDetail.description:
Body of `GET /api/servers/{id}`: the listing row plus the agent's
current certificate.

next_cursor.description: Pass as `cursor` for the next page; `null` on the last one.

ServerView.description:
One server. Field names and types are part of the API contract: add
fields, never rename or remove them.

agent_version.description: Version reported by the live stream, else the one last stored.

cert_not_after.description:
Latest expiry among the agent's unrevoked certificates; `null` when
it has none. Past dates mean every certificate has expired.

command_kinds.description:
What its agent last said it does with each command kind: `accepted`,
`off` or `unsupported` (ADR-0076). `null`, or a kind missing here, is
unknown: its agent or a relay on the way does not report yet.

connected_at.description: Start of the current stream, when online.

last_heartbeat.description:
Last message received: from the live stream when online, else the
last time recorded in the database.

offline_alerts.description:
Whether it opens an incident when offline (ADR-0072); muted when
this or `site_offline_alerts` is `false`.

open_incidents.description: Threshold and offline incidents currently open on this server.

package_updates.description: Whether the host can take package updates and sources (ADR-0063).

silenced_until.description: While a silence covers it, when the last one ends (ADR-0079).

via_relay.description: Peer ID of the relay carrying the live stream, if any.

Shell.description: The shell that runs a server's commands, which decides the rules.

target_id.description: The server, relay, site or customer; absent for `all`.

can_end.description: Whether this user may end it.

agent_auto_update.description:
The site's automatic update override: `null` follows the
server-wide setting (ADR-0055).

agent_auto_update_effective.description: Whether automatic updates apply to the site, override or not.

offline_alerts.description:
Whether servers and relays of the site open incidents when offline
(ADR-0072).

relay_count.description: Enrolled relays of the site, revoked ones included (ADR-0029).

SnapshotSupport.description:
Whether the server can be snapshotted; without it the interface shows
that rollback is limited.

detail.description:
With `cannot_snapshot`: what Proxmox cannot snapshot, like "rootfs
is on storage local (dir), which cannot take snapshots".

oneOf.description: The mapped guest's kind, so the reason can say VM or container.

left_out.description: What a snapshot does not hold, though Proxmox takes one.

method.description:
Which snapshot a change gets when available: `proxmox`, or a local
`lvm` or `zfs` snapshot (ADR-0094).

Tier.description: Risk tiers of architecture §8, from least to most dangerous.

tags.name: remediation
tags.description: Commands the AI proposed, waiting for a person

tags.name: metrics
tags.description: Metric queries built by MonitorFlow, never raw PromQL

tags.name: campaigns
tags.description: Package or agent updates sent to many servers of one customer, in batches (`waves`), inside maintenance windows, stopping when a batch fails more than its failure threshold. Targets are frozen when the campaign is made; nothing is sent before it is started. Every server gets a signed command of its own, `apply_updates` (or `self_update` for an agent update campaign), queued behind any other command of that server and checked by its agent, which runs package updates only when its administrator allowed them. Campaign commands are made by an administrator, not the AI: the risk rules and the approval queue do not apply to them. Reading needs a role on the customer as a whole (everything or the customer); creating and acting need an administrator role on it. Needs the key area "updates".
